title: Casebook: longform context-bleed and repetition failure signals
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working casebook for a set of onboarding eval failures observed in the longform summarization promptset (seeded from customer pilot workloads). Focus: two correlated failure signals that repeatedly trigger regressions after model swaps or quantization changes: (1) context-bleed (model re-using unrelated earlier context when producing later sections) and (2) emergent repetition/refrain loops in multi-paragraph outputs. Goal: summarize observed clusters, hypothesize root causes, propose quick mitigations and a medium-term evaluation + fix plan.

High-level summary (drive-by):
- Observed across 3 model variants during onboarding (fp16 baseline, int8-quant candidate, and a 4-bit quantized experimental build).
- Error often appears on long inputs (>2500 tokens) or when prompts include interleaved instruction + examples + long reference text.
- Failure modes: non-sequitur injection from earlier examples (context-bleed) and repeated paragraph-level refrains (exact or near-exact repeated sentences).
- Impact: coherence loss >10% on our longform ROUGE/QA checks; customer-facing severity (pilot) — outputs judged as "nonsensical" or "spammy" in 18/120 sampled cases.

Data and promptset notes:
- Promptset: longform_summ_2024_v3 (120 prompts, mix of meeting transcripts, policy documents, and multi-article synthesis tasks).
- Example prompt structure most affected: system instruction -> 2 short examples -> long source text -> explicit section-by-section generation instruction.
- Inputs where failure spikes: long transcripts with repeated speaker tokens, and concatenated articles where entity disambiguation is weak.

Observed signal clusters (rough clustering from manual review + kmeans on embedding features):
1) Context-bleed (cluster CB):
   - Symptom: model injects sentences referring to earlier examples or unrelated passage (e.g., "As shown above in the product roadmap example..." when no roadmap exists in source).
   - Frequency: ~30% of failures on inputs >3000 tokens; also present at ~8% for 1800-3000 token range.
   - Proto examples: 3 short excerpts included as anonymized snippets in linked PR (github:repo/PR#1428).

2) Refrain/repetition loops (cluster RL):
   - Symptom: blocks of 1–3 sentences repeat verbatim or with trivial variants every 2–3 paragraphs; often starts after an instruction to "summarize in sections".
   - Frequency: high for int8 candidate; lower but present on fp16 baseline after long sequences (>3500 tokens).

3) Hyphen/format bleed (cluster HF):
   - Symptom: tokenization artifacts that cause repeated hyphen bullets or spurious list markers which trigger the model to restart earlier sections. Appears correlated with tokenizer boundary handling for certain punctuation.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: KV-cache/addressing drift during large context (kernel scheduling + quantization noise). When past keys/values are slightly corrupted, attention weights incorrectly promote earlier positions, producing explicit references to them.
- H2: Repeated-example priming: few-shot examples embed strong structural templates; model overapplies example-level formatting leading to literal repetition when generation boundary signals are weak.
- H3: Top-p/top-k sampling interplay in batched microsecond-scheduled decoding (different RNG seeds/temperature across micro-batches) causing sticky loops on particular token subsequences, exacerbated by quantization.
- H4: Tokenizer misalignment for concatenated inputs creates phantom tokens that the model interprets as section separators; these tokens trigger learned "section headers" causing content duplication.

Priority quick mitigations (can be rolled within onboarding config or runtime policy):
1) Prompt surgery (immediate, low risk):
   - Remove inline few-shot examples for the longform_summ_2024_v3 cases; move examples to separate adapter prompt or to model instruction only (no example text in main context).
   - Add explicit "Do not reference previous examples" guard clause early in system instruction.
2) Forced de-duplication post-process (stateless):
   - Run a cheap post-decoder dedupe pass that collapses verbatim repeated n-grams (n=8) and heuristic paraphrase repeats (fuzzy match) across paragraph boundaries. Not perfect but reduces user-visible loopiness.
3) Decoder hyperparams tweak for quant candidates:
   - Lower top-p by 0.05 and increase repetition penalty by +0.8 for int8/4bit candidate runs during release gating. Track regression delta.
4) Batching isolation toggle:
   - For longform lanes, isolate micro-batches so each request uses a fresh RNG/decoding stream (avoids cross-request seed interference seen in some runtime configs).

Medium-term fixes (investigation + infra changes):
- KV cache integrity checks: instrument and add checksum sampling for KV tensors post-quantization kernel to detect drift. If checksum deviation > threshold, trigger rerun on FP fallback path.
- Tokenizer normalization: add a pre-pass that normalizes repeated punctuation and canonicalizes speaker tokens in transcripts (strip repeated tokens >3).
- Example templating guidelines: define a templating library that ensures examples are demarcated with an explicit sentinel token that the model recognizes as "do not copy into output" during training/instruction tuning.
- Decoding model patches: explore attention re-normalization layers to reduce spurious high-attention mass to far past positions (low-level model surgery). This is more invasive and requires bench/ablation.

Evaluation plan and metrics to validate mitigations:
- Short-list 200 high-risk prompts from longform_summ_2024_v3 (stratified by input length and doc type).
- Automated checks: paragraph-level BLEU/ROUGE but also new coherence metric: cross-paragraph token overlap ratio (target < 0.02). Monitor fraction of outputs with repeated n-grams >=8.
- Human eval: pairwise A/B on top 50 failure seeds, judgeers label: coherent/acceptable/unsafe. Aim to reduce "unacceptable" by 60% for candidate.
- Rolling gate: require that candidate with mitigations reduces CB+RL cluster incidence by >=40% vs baseline before onboarding approval.

Notes from quick manual triage (team observations):
- Ahmed: saw identical repeat pattern on 2 different customers - likely model-side not data-specific.
- Marina: tokenizer normalizer reduced HF cluster on a quick pass for 12/20 samples.
- Diego: checksum instrumentation prototype shows occasional 0.3% bit flips after int8 kernel; needs more sampling.

Open questions / risks:
- Is the repeat primarily a decoding artifact or a learned behavior that surfaces with noisy KV caches? Need controlled ablation (same model, swap decoding stacks).
- Post-processing dedupe could mask a deeper correctness problem (we need to avoid changing meaning).
- Gate turnaround time: some mitigations (e.g., hyperparam changes + prompt surgery) can be shipped in days; KV integrity + decoder patches will take weeks-months.

Immediate next steps (owners + ETA):
- Prompt surgery + guard clause: Priya (owner) -> PR + test harness by 2024-11-17.
- Post-process dedupe prototype: Ahmed -> experiment branch + eval by 2024-11-22.
- Tokenizer normalization script: Marina -> iterate, report 2024-11-20.
- KV checksum sampling in runtime: Diego -> prototype telemetry in infra by 2024-12-01.

Notes-to-self / TODOs:
- Add anonymized snippets to this doc (need legal sign-off) before wider sharing.
- File a follow-up Confluence page with the deterministic ablation plan.

Appendix: selected anonymized example (high-level paraphrase)
- Input: 12,000-word conference transcript + 2 short examples.
- Observed failure: paragraph 4 references "the roadmap example above" which is only present in the few-shot example (should not be referenced). Model later repeats an earlier sentence verbatim at paragraph 7, 10 and 13.
- Quick local fix: removing examples eliminated the explicit "roadmap" reference but repetition persisted at lower frequency.

If you iterate on this doc, append notes under an "edits" timestamped list so we can trace hypotheses -> results.

End of casebook entry (draft).
